summary: Source decomposition of the certified-solution toolchain from four primary works not in the supplied library, fetched as authorized public copies: Tzanakis-de Weger, On the practical solution of the Thue equation (J. Number Theory 1989); McCallum-Poonen, The method of Chabauty and Coleman (2012, author copy); Bruin-Stoll, The Mordell-Weil sieve (arXiv 0906.1934v2); and Balakrishnan-Dogra-Muller-Tuitman-Vonk, Quadratic Chabauty for modular curves (arXiv 2101.01862v4). ED.1/ED.2 follow the Thue method: large solutions approximate a real root (Lemma 1.1), the unit equation gives a small linear form in logarithms (Lemma 1.2), an explicit Baker-type lower bound gives a huge bound (Lemmas 2.1-2.4), and LLL reduction (Propositions 3.1-3.2) brings it down. This yields the four-class exhaustiveness certificate. ED.4 covers the p-adic logarithm, Lemma 4.2, Chabauty's theorem (proof omitted in the source), residue-class integrals, the Newton-polygon Lemma 5.1, Coleman's bound (Theorem 5.3) and its bad-reduction version (Theorem A.5). ED.5 covers the sieve set A(S, N), its soundness, staged computation, coset separation by canonical height, the genus-2 Kummer test, and the Chabauty-plus-sieve procedure, whose termination is conjectural. ED.6 covers the quadratic Chabauty hypotheses (r = g, log isomorphism, rk NS >= 2), Betts-Dogra local heights, Algorithm 3.12 with its FAIL conditions, and the precision bounds; ED.0 gets the certified p-adic root-isolation Lemma 4.7. ED.3 is represented only by the saturation index test. All stages remain partial: LLL, de Weger's thesis, Waldschmidt's constants, descent/rank algorithms, Coleman 1985, Stoll's papers and the quadratic Chabauty foundations (BD18, BDM+19, BD19) are imports that were not read.

nodes.title: Certified determination of the roots of a p-adic power series in a disc from finitely many truncated coefficients (BDMTV Lemma 4.7)
nodes.statement: Let F(x) = sum_{i>=0} F_i x^i in Q_p[[x]], and suppose there are integers k, m, n with min{ord_p(F_i) + i : i >= 0} = k and max{i >= 0 : ord_p(F_i) + i = n} < m. Suppose moreover that F has at most d roots in the closed disc {ord_p(x) >= 1}. Then the roots of F in that disc can be determined, with multiplicity, to precision (n - k)/d by computing F_0, ..., F_{m-1} modulo p^n.
hypotheses: F in Q_p[[x]] with the two integer conditions on ord_p(F_i) + i
an a priori bound d on the number of roots in {ord_p(x) >= 1} (e.g. from a Newton-polygon or Chabauty-type count)
proofSteps: F(px) lies in p^k Z_p[[x]] but not in p^{k+1} Z_p[[x]], so G(x) = p^{-k} F(px) lies in Z_p[[x]] minus pZ_p[[x]].
For every alpha in Z_p the positive slopes of the Newton polygon of G(x + alpha) are determined by the first m coefficients (by the hypothesis on n and m).

If G is congruent modulo p^{n-k} to a polynomial H in Z_p[x] with a root alpha of multiplicity e, the first e coefficients of G(x + alpha) have valuation at least n - k. Since G(x + alpha) has degree <= m mod p^{n-k} and a coefficient of valuation zero, its Newton polygon has a segment of slope >= (n-k)/d of length at least e.
Remark 4.8: in practice d = 1 after recentering and rescaling, so precision loss comes from k.
acceptance: This is a disc certificate in the sense of ED.0: the output is an explicit p-adic precision (n-k)/d, and numerical agreement of approximate roots is not used.
Check on F(x) = x(x - p) (roots 0 and p in the disc): with truncation at m = 3 the lemma should separate them only when (n - k)/d exceeds 1.

nodes.title: Tzanakis-de Weger Proposition 3.1: an LLL reduction replaces an exponent bound K_3 for |Lambda_0| < K_1 exp(-K_2 A) by a bound of size log K_3
nodes.statement: Let mu_1, ..., mu_q be real numbers, linearly independent over Q (q >= 2), Lambda = a_1 mu_1 + ... + a_q mu_q with (a_1, ..., a_q) in Z^q (the homogeneous case delta = 0), A = max |a_i|, and K_1, K_2, K_3 > 0. Consider the solutions of (3.1): |Lambda| < K_1 exp(-K_2 A) and A <= K_3. Choose c_0 somewhat larger than K_3^q and let Gamma be the lattice spanned by the columns of the q x q matrix with identity in the first q-1 rows and last row ([c_0 mu_1], ..., [c_0 mu_q]) ([.] = nearest integer). Let b_1, ..., b_q be an LLL-reduced basis. If |b_1| > sqrt((q^2 + q - 1) 2^{q-1}) K_3, then every solution of (3.1) satisfies A < (1/K_2) (log(c_0 K_1) - log(sqrt(2^{-(q-1)} |b_1|^2 - (q-1) K_3^2) - q K_3)).
hypotheses: mu_i real and Q-linearly independent (case (i)); homogeneous form delta = 0
K_1, K_2 small and K_3 very large known constants (in the Thue application from Lemmas 2.2 and 2.4)
c_0 chosen with c_0 of size K_3^q so that the hypothesis on |b_1| holds in practice
proofSteps: For a solution, the lattice point A . (a_1, ..., a_q)^T = (a_1, ..., a_{q-1}, lambda_0) with lambda_0 = sum a_i [c_0 mu_i] satisfies |lambda_0 - c_0 Lambda| <= q A < q K_3, so |lambda_0| < c_0 |Lambda| + q K_3 (3.3).
By the LLL lower bound (3.2), a_1^2 + ... + a_{q-1}^2 + lambda_0^2 >= l_0^2, hence (q-1) K_3^2 + lambda_0^2 >= l_0^2.

Combining gives c_0 |Lambda| + q K_3 >= sqrt(l_0^2 - (q-1) K_3^2), i.e. c_0 |Lambda| > sigma_3 K_3 in the notation of the source; with |Lambda| < K_1 exp(-K_2 A) this yields the logarithmic bound on A.

Heuristic justification that |b_1| is of size K_3 (so the hypothesis usually holds): the basis is almost orthogonal and the lattice has covolume |c_0 mu_q| of size K_3^q. This is a heuristic, not a proof; if the hypothesis fails, change c_0.
acceptance: The reduction can be iterated with the new bound in place of K_3.
Failure mode: if the mu_i are Q-dependent, b_1 is very short and the hypothesis fails; use case (iii) (reduce to an independent subset with an integer relation).
Certificate content for ED.1: the lattice basis, the reduced basis b_1, the check of the |b_1| inequality in exact arithmetic, and the resulting bound.

nodes.title: Tzanakis-de Weger Proposition 3.2: in the inhomogeneous case delta != 0, the distance from (0, ..., 0, -[c_0 delta]) to the lattice gives A < (1/K_2) log(c_0 K_1/(q K_3))
nodes.statement: Let Lambda = delta + a_1 mu_1 + ... + a_q mu_q with delta != 0 and Gamma, c_0, b_1, ..., b_q as in the homogeneous case, B the matrix of the reduced basis. Let x = (0, ..., 0, -[c_0 delta])^T in Z^q with coordinates s_1, ..., s_q with respect to b_1, ..., b_q (s = B^{-1} x), and i* = max{i : 1 <= i <= q, s_i not in Z}. If 2^{-(q-1)/2} ||s_{i*}|| |b_1| > sqrt(4q^2 + 3q - 3/4) K_3 (||.|| the distance to the nearest integer), then every solution of (3.1) with delta != 0 satisfies A < (1/K_2) log(c_0 K_1/(q K_3)).
hypotheses: mu_i Q-linearly independent, delta != 0
the change-of-basis matrix U with B = A_matrix U and its inverse computed exactly by the integral LLL
imports: de Weger, Algorithms for Diophantine equations [32], Lemma 3.5 (l(x, Gamma) >= 2^{-(q-1)/2} ||s_{i*}|| |b_1|) and the argument of its Lemma 3.7
proofSteps: Imported: by Lemma 3.5 of de Weger [32], the minimal distance l(x, Gamma) of x to Gamma satisfies l(x, Gamma) >= 2^{-(q-1)/2} ||s_{i*}|| |b_1| (not read here).

By hypothesis l(x, Gamma) > sqrt(4q^2 + 3q - 3/4) K_3. Arguing "similarly as in Lemma 3.7 of [32]" (not read here), if l(x, Gamma) > sqrt(4q^2 + 3q - 3/4) X_0 then |Lambda| > K_1 exp(-K_2 A) has no solution with (1/K_2) log(c_0 K_1/(q X_0)) <= A <= X_0. Taking X_0 = K_3 gives the bound.
If ||s_{i*}|| is too small, try another c_0 or use Lemma 3.6 of [32] instead of Lemma 3.5.
acceptance: This is the "closest-vector certificate" demanded by ED.1: the exported data are x, the coordinates s, i*, ||s_{i*}||, |b_1| and the inequality check.

nodes.title: Tzanakis-de Weger Lemma 1.1: for |Y| > Y_0 (resp. > Y_1), beta = X - xi Y is tiny at one real embedding (resp. X/Y is a continued-fraction convergent)
nodes.statement: Let F(X, Y) = sum f_i X^{n-i} Y^i in Z[X, Y] be an irreducible binary form of degree n >= 3, m a nonzero integer, g(x) = F(x, 1) with s >= 1 real roots xi^(1), ..., xi^(s) and t pairs of complex roots, and K = Q(xi). For a solution of F(X, Y) = m put beta = X - xi Y in K. With Y_0 = [(2^{n-1}|m| / (min_{1<=i<=t} |g'(xi^(s+i))| . min_{1<=i<=t} |Im xi^(s+i)|))^{1/n}] if t >= 1 and Y_0 = 1 if t = 0, C_1 = 2^{n-1}|m|/min_{1<=i<=s}|g'(xi^(i))|, C_2 = (1/2) min_{1<=i<j<=n} |xi^(i) - xi^(j)|, and Y_1 = max(Y_0, [(4 C_1)^{1/(n-2)}]): (i) if |Y| > Y_0 there is i_0 in {1, ..., s} with |beta^(i_0)| <= C_1 |Y|^{-(n-1)} and |beta^(i)| >= C_2 |Y| for i != i_0; (ii) if |Y| > Y_1 then X/Y is a convergent of the continued fraction expansion of xi^(i_0).
hypotheses: F irreducible over Q of degree n >= 3 with at least one real root (otherwise small bounds are trivial)
proofSteps: Choose i_0 minimizing |beta^(i)|. For all i, |Y| |xi^(i) - xi^(i_0)| = |beta^(i) - beta^(i_0)| <= 2|beta^(i)|, so |beta^(i)| >= C_2 |Y|.
From |m| = |f_0| prod |beta^(i)| and |beta^(i)| >= (1/2)|Y||xi^(i) - xi^(i_0)| one gets |beta^(i_0)| <= 2^{n-1}|m| /(|g'(xi^(i_0))| |Y|^{n-1}).
If i_0 > s (a nonreal root), |beta^(i_0)| >= |Im xi^(i_0)| |Y|, which is impossible for |Y| > Y_0; so i_0 is real, giving (i).
If |Y| > Y_1 then |X/Y - xi^(i_0)| < 1/(2|Y|^2), and Legendre's criterion (Hardy-Wright Theorem 184) gives (ii).
acceptance: This fixes the "small solutions" class Y_1 < |Y| <= Y_2 as convergents, which are finitely many below any bound and can be enumerated with a certificate.
Check on x^3 - 2y^3 = 1 that the solution (1, 0) and (-1, -1) are handled by the "very small" class |Y| <= Y_1.

nodes.title: Tzanakis-de Weger Lemma 1.2 and (1.3)-(1.4): a large Thue solution gives a linear form Lambda in logarithms of units with |Lambda| < 1.39 C_1 C_3/C_2 |Y|^{-n}
nodes.statement: In the setting of Lemma 1.1 with i_0 real, choose j, k with i_0, j, k pairwise distinct and either j, k in {1, ..., s} (real case) or j + t = k (complex case). Put Lambda = log|((xi^(i_0) - xi^(j))/(xi^(i_0) - xi^(k))) (beta^(k)/beta^(j))| in the real case and Lambda = (1/i) Log(...) in the complex case (so Lambda is real and |Lambda| <= pi). With C_3 = max_{i_1,i_2,i_3 distinct} |(xi^(i_1) - xi^(i_2))/(xi^(i_1) - xi^(i_3))| and Y_1* = max(Y_1, [(2 C_1 C_3/C_2)^{1/n}]), Lemma 1.2: if |Y| > Y_1* then |Lambda| < (1.39 C_1 C_3/C_2) |Y|^{-n}. Writing beta = mu epsilon_1^{a_1} ... epsilon_r^{a_r} with epsilon_i fundamental units of an order R of K (r = s + t - 1) and mu from a finite complete set M of nonassociated elements of norm m/f_0, Lambda becomes the linear form (1.3) Lambda = log|((xi^(i_0)-xi^(j))/(xi^(i_0)-xi^(k))) (mu^(k)/mu^(j))| + sum a_i log|epsilon_i^(k)/epsilon_i^(j)| in the real case, or (1.4) with arguments and an extra term a_0 . 2 pi in the complex case.
hypotheses: F irreducible of degree n >= 3 with s >= 1 real roots
a system of fundamental units epsilon_1, ..., epsilon_r of an order R of K is known
a complete set of nonassociated mu with f_0 N(mu) = m is known (the source does not treat these computations)
proofSteps: Eliminating X and Y from beta^(i) = X - Y xi^(i) for i = i_0, j, k gives the unit relation (1.2), whose right-hand side is at most C_1 C_3/C_2 |Y|^{-n} by Lemma 1.1, so |e^Lambda - 1| < C_1 C_3/C_2 |Y|^{-n} < 1/2.

Real case: |e^Lambda - 1| < 1/2 implies |Lambda| <= 2 log 2 |e^Lambda - 1| <= 1.39 |e^Lambda - 1|. Complex case: |e^{i Lambda} - 1| = 2|sin(Lambda/2)| < 1/2 gives |Lambda| <= (1/2)/sin(1/4) |sin(Lambda/2)| <= 1.02 |e^{i Lambda} - 1|.
The fundamental units and the finite set M reduce (1.1) to finitely many unit equations beta = mu epsilon^a; substituting gives (1.3)/(1.4) with integer unknowns a_i.
acceptance: Nonvanishing: beta^(i_0) != 0 and (1.2) imply Lambda != 0 (used in Lemma 2.4 before applying the logarithmic-form lower bound).

nodes.statement: Let A = max_{1<=i<=r} |a_i|. Lemma 2.1: for I = {h_1, ..., h_r} in {1, ..., n} put U_I = (log|epsilon_i^(h_l)|)_{i,l}, N[U_I^{-1}] = max_i sum_l |u_il| for U_I^{-1} = (u_il), mu_- = min_{mu in M, i} |mu^(i)|, mu_+ = max_{mu in M, i} |mu^(i)|, C_4 = (1/2 + max_{i_1<i_2} |xi^(i_1) - xi^(i_2)|)/mu_- and C_5 = min((n-1) min_I N[U_I^{-1}], max_I N[U_I^{-1}]). If |Y| > Y_1 then A <= C_5 log(C_4 |Y|). Lemma 2.2: with C_6 = 1.39 C_1 C_3 C_4^n/C_2 and Y_2' = max(Y_1*, 2|m|^{1/n}, mu_+/C_2), if |Y| > Y_2' then |Lambda| < C_6 exp(-(n/C_5) A).
hypotheses: as in Lemmas 1.1-1.2, with fundamental units and the finite set M fixed
proofSteps: From beta = mu epsilon^a, the vector (log|beta^(h)/mu^(h)|)_h equals U_I^T a (2.1), so A <= N[U_I^{-1}] max_h |log|beta^(h)/mu^(h)||.
Using the end of the proof of Lemma 1.1, |beta^(h)|/|mu^(h)| < C_4 |Y| for all h, and C_4 |Y| > 1 (2.2).
For i with |beta^(i)/mu^(i)| < 1, the product formula prod_h |beta^(h)/mu^(h)| = 1 gives |log|beta^(i)/mu^(i)|| < (n-1) log(C_4|Y|) (2.3); this gives A <= (n-1) min_I N[U_I^{-1}] log(C_4|Y|).
Choosing I with i_0 not in I, Lemma 1.1 gives |beta^(h)/mu^(h)| > C_2 |Y|/mu_+ > 1 for h in I, so A <= max_I N[U_I^{-1}] log(C_4|Y|).
Lemma 2.2 substitutes |Y| >= exp(A/C_5)/C_4 into Lemma 1.2.
acceptance: Check that C_5 uses the minimum of the two estimates, which the proof establishes separately.

nodes.statement: Lemma 2.3 (Waldschmidt [30], imported): if Lambda != 0 then |Lambda| > exp(-C_7 (log A + C_8)) in the real case; in the complex case the same holds with A replaced by A' = max_{0<=i<=r} |a_i|, and since |a_0| < 1/2 + (1/2) r A + 0.51/(2 pi) r A for A >= 2 one may use A with C_8' = C_8 + log r (C_8' = C_8 in the real case). Lemma 2.4: with C_9 = (2 C_5/n)(log C_6 + C_7 C_8' + C_7 log(C_5 C_7/n)), if |Y| > Y_2' then A < C_9.
hypotheses: Lambda != 0 (proved in the source from beta^(i_0) != 0 and (1.2))
explicit constants C_7, C_8 of Waldschmidt's theorem as computed in Appendix II of the source (not read here)
imported elementary lemma: Petho-de Weger [20] Lemma 2.3 turning A <= (C_5/n)(log C_6 + C_7 C_8' + C_7 log A) into A < C_9
proofSteps: |e^Lambda - 1| < 1/2 (real) or |e^{i Lambda} - 1| < 1/2 (complex) and beta^(i_0) != 0 give Lambda != 0 via (1.2).
Lemmas 2.2 and 2.3 give exp(-C_7(log A + C_8')) < |Lambda| < C_6 exp(-(n/C_5) A), i.e. A < (C_5/n)(log C_6 + C_7 C_8' + C_7 log A).

nodes.title: Tzanakis-de Weger method: every solution of F(X, Y) = m lies in one of four explicitly bounded classes, each closed by its own certificate
nodes.statement: Let F be an irreducible binary form of degree n >= 3 with at least one real root of F(x, 1), and m != 0. There are explicit reals Y_1 < Y_2 < Y_3 such that the solutions of F(X, Y) = m split into four classes: (I) very small solutions |Y| <= Y_1, found by enumeration; (II) small solutions Y_1 < |Y| <= Y_2, found among the continued fraction convergents of the real roots xi^(i) (Lemma 1.1(ii)); (III) large solutions Y_2 < |Y| <= Y_3, shown not to exist by lattice reduction; (IV) very large solutions |Y| > Y_3, shown not to exist by the theory of linear forms in logarithms. Y_1 comes from Lemma 1.1, Y_3 from the logarithmic-form bound (Lemma 2.4), and Y_2 from the reduced bound of Section II.3.
hypotheses: F irreducible of degree >= 3 with a real root; m != 0
fundamental units and a complete set M of nonassociated mu of norm m/f_0 are known
the reduction hypotheses of Propositions 3.1/3.2 hold for some choice of c_0, or case (iii) is applied
proofSteps: Class (IV): Lemma 2.4 gives A < C_9 for |Y| > Y_2'; with A <= C_5 log(C_4|Y|) and Lemma 2.1 this yields an explicit Y_3 (the source notes this "can be derived easily" and does not write it out).
Class (III): apply Proposition 3.1 (delta = 0) or 3.2 (delta != 0), possibly iterated, with K_1 = C_6, K_2 = n/C_5 and K_3 = C_9, to reduce the bound on A, and translate back to a bound Y_2 on |Y|.
Class (II): for Y_1 < |Y| <= Y_2, X/Y is a convergent of the continued fraction of a real root (Lemma 1.1(ii)), so finitely many candidates are checked.
Class (I): enumerate |Y| <= Y_1.

Only then is it proved that every solution lies in the enumerated set.
Worked test from the source: Section III solves the elliptic curve arising from Mohanty's problem via two quartic Thue equations over a totally real quartic field (not decomposed here).
S-unit and Thue-Mahler instances need the p-adic analogue (Tzanakis-de Weger, How to explicitly solve a Thue-Mahler equation, reference [29]), which was not read.

nodes.title: A finite-index subgroup G of J(Q) whose index is prime to the relevant primes can replace J(Q) in Chabauty and sieve computations; the index is certified prime to l by reduction maps
nodes.statement: Let X/Q be a curve of genus g >= 2 with Jacobian J. (1) (McCallum-Poonen Remark 6.1) For Chabauty-type arguments at p it suffices to know explicit generators of a finite-index subgroup G of J(Q) with the same p-adic closure in J(Q_p). Any G of index prime to p . #J(F_p) has this property. (2) If G is known to have finite index, one can usually verify that the index is not divisible by a given prime l by finding a homomorphism J(Q) -> B to a finite abelian group B killed by l such that the induced map G/lG -> B is injective. In practice B is a product of J(F_q)/lJ(F_q) over a few primes q of good reduction. (3) (Bruin-Stoll) For the Mordell-Weil sieve it suffices to know generators of a finite-index subgroup whose index is coprime to a certain set of primes (in the Chabauty combination, coprime to N), and this can be checked with local information only.
hypotheses: G subset of J(Q) of finite index (finiteness itself requires knowing rank J(Q), e.g. from a descent)
for (2): primes q of good reduction with J(Q) -> J(F_q)/l J(F_q) computable on G
proofSteps: Source status: stated as remarks with a one-sentence justification; no proof is written in either source.

Unwritten justification of (2): if l divided (J(Q) : G), some element of J(Q) outside G would have its l-th multiple in G, making G/lG -> J(Q)/lJ(Q) non-injective; since G/lG -> B factors through J(Q)/lJ(Q), injectivity of G/lG -> B excludes this. This deduction is not written in McCallum-Poonen and should be checked, including the role of torsion.
acceptance: Worked check: on a rank-1 genus-2 Jacobian, verify that a known point P of infinite order plus torsion has index prime to N by the reduction test before running the sieve (Bruin-Stoll 4.4).

Acceptance for ED.3: this is only the saturation part. The rank certification (descent upper bound plus independent points) and the saturation at all primes up to a height-derived bound are not covered by the sources read.

nodes.title: The abelian integral eta_J(Q) = int_0^Q omega_J on J(Q_p), the pairing J(Q_p) x H^0(J_{Q_p}, Omega^1) -> Q_p, and log : J(Q_p) -> T as a local diffeomorphism
nodes.statement: Let J be the Jacobian of a curve X/Q of genus g >= 2 with an embedding iota : X -> J, P -> [P - O], for a known O in X(Q). For omega_J in H^0(J_{Q_p}, Omega^1) (a g-dimensional Q_p-space) there is a unique map eta_J : J(Q_p) -> Q_p, Q -> int_0^Q omega_J, such that (a) eta_J is a homomorphism, and (b) on some open subgroup U of J(Q_p) it is computed by expanding omega_J in local coordinates, integrating formally and evaluating. One may take U = J^1(Q_p), the kernel of reduction J(Q_p) -> J(F_p), with J(F_p) the F_p-points of the special fibre of the Neron model in general. This gives a bilinear pairing J(Q_p) x H^0(J_{Q_p}, Omega^1) -> Q_p and a homomorphism log : J(Q_p) -> T, T the dual of H^0(J_{Q_p}, Omega^1), whose derivative at 0 is the identity, so log is a local diffeomorphism.
hypotheses: X smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g >= 2 over Q with a known rational point O (or a rational divisor of positive degree d, Remark 2.1)
for bad reduction: the Neron model of J over Z_p and its formal group
proofSteps: Existence and uniqueness of eta_J use translation invariance of omega_J; the facts are quoted from Bourbaki, Lie groups III Section 7.6.

Remark 4.1: the Neron model of J is smooth over Z_p; completing along the zero section gives a smooth formal group whose points are J^1(Q_p), and Bourbaki III Section 7.6 Prop. 14(ii) gives convergence of the antiderivative there.
The derivative of log at 0 is the identity T -> T.
acceptance: Check on an elliptic curve with good reduction that log restricted to E^1(Q_p) is the formal logarithm.

There is an open subgroup U of J(Q_p) such that if Q in U, then int_0^Q omega_J can be computed by expanding omega_J in power series in local coordinates

nodes.title: McCallum-Poonen Lemma 4.2: r' = dim of the p-adic closure of J(Q) is at most r = rank J(Q)
nodes.statement: Let Jbar(Q) be the closure of J(Q) in J(Q_p) (an analytic subgroup), r' = dim Jbar(Q) and r = rank J(Q). Then r' <= r. More precisely r' = rank_{Z_p}(Z_p log J(Q)) <= rank_Z log J(Q) <= rank_Z J(Q) = r, where the second inequality is an equality because log has finite kernel; the first can be strict, and r' <= g always.
hypotheses: X/Q of genus g >= 2 with Jacobian J; p a prime
proofSteps: r' = dim Jbar(Q) = dim log(Jbar(Q)) since log is a local diffeomorphism.
log is continuous and Jbar(Q) is compact, so log(Jbar(Q)) is the closure of log J(Q).
The closure of a subgroup of Q_p^g is its Z_p-span, giving (3).
acceptance: Remark 4.3: r > g is possible while r' <= g, so r' < r can occur; check the inequality chain on a rank-2 genus-2 example.

nodes.title: Integrals on X via the Jacobian, their vanishing on torsion and rational classes, and power-series expansion on residue classes (McCallum-Poonen 5.1-5.2, 5.4)
nodes.statement: Assume X has good reduction at p (generic fibre of a smooth proper curve over Z_p). Restriction H^0(J_{Q_p}, Omega^1) -> H^0(X_{Q_p}, Omega^1) is an isomorphism; for omega_J restricting to omega set int_Q^{Q'} omega := int_0^{[Q' - Q]} omega_J. Properties: (i) if sum (Q'_i - Q_i) is a principal divisor, or [sum (Q'_i - Q_i)] is torsion in J(Q_p), then sum int_{Q_i}^{Q'_i} omega = 0; (ii) if Q, Q' have the same reduction in X(F_p), int_Q^{Q'} omega is computed by expanding in a local parameter t. For a residue class over Qtilde in X(F_p) and t reducing to a uniformizer at Qtilde: (1) t maps the residue class bijectively to pZ_p; (2) if omega is normalized to reduce to omega-tilde != 0, then omega = w(t)dt with w in Z_p[[t]] nonzero mod p; (3) eta = int_O omega is represented on the class by I(t) in Q_p[[t]] with I' = w. If r' < g, a nonzero functional lambda : T -> Q_p vanishing on log J(Q) gives omega_J with eta_J = lambda o log vanishing on J(Q), hence (iii): if [sum (Q'_i - Q_i)] is in J(Q), then sum int omega = 0.
hypotheses: p a prime of good reduction for X
O in X(Q) as base point
for (iii): r' < g
proofSteps: The restriction isomorphism is quoted from Milne, Jacobian varieties, Prop. 2.2 (not read).
Properties (i)-(ii) follow from the corresponding properties of eta_J (homomorphism, kills torsion; local expansion on U).
Facts (1)-(3) on residue classes are stated with "one can show" (Hensel-type arguments); no proof is written in the source.
Section 5.4: log J(Q) is a Z_p-module of rank r' in T = Q_p^g; if r' < g a nonzero lambda vanishing on it exists, and eta_J = lambda o log.

nodes.title: McCallum-Poonen Lemma 5.1: if f'(t) in Z_p[[t]] has m = ord_{t=0}(f' mod p) < p - 2, then f has at most m + 1 zeros in pZ_p
nodes.statement: Let f(t) in Q_p[[t]] with f'(t) in Z_p[[t]], and m = ord_{t=0}(f'(t) mod p). If m < p - 2, then f has at most m + 1 zeros in pZ_p. Remark 5.2 (variants stated without proof): Coleman gives an estimate without conditions on p and over any p-adic field; if moreover the coefficient of t^{p-1} in f'(t) is in pZ_p, then m < 2p - 2 suffices.
hypotheses: f'(t) in Z_p[[t]]
m < p - 2
proofSteps: Write f = sum a_i t^i. The hypotheses give v(a_{m+1}) = 0 and v(a_i) >= -v_p(i) > m + 1 - i for i > m + 1.
So the Newton polygon of f has no slopes <= -1 to the right of (m+1, 0), and Newton polygon theory (Koblitz, p-adic numbers, IV.4) gives at most m + 1 zeros in pZ_p.
acceptance: Check the inequality -v_p(i) > m + 1 - i for i > m + 1 when m < p - 2 (it fails for large m relative to p, which is why the hypothesis is needed).

nodes.title: Coleman's theorem (McCallum-Poonen Theorem 5.3): residue-class bounds m + 1 and, for p > 2g, #X(Q) <= #X(F_p) + 2g - 2
nodes.statement: Let X/Q have genus g >= 2 with Jacobian J, p a prime of good reduction, and r' < g. (a) Let omega != 0 in H^0(X_{Q_p}, Omega^1) satisfy (i)-(iii), scaled to reduce to omega-tilde != 0 in H^0(X_{F_p}, Omega^1). For Qtilde in X(F_p) with m = ord_Qtilde(omega-tilde) < p - 2, at most m + 1 points of X(Q) reduce to Qtilde. (b) If p > 2g, then #X(Q) <= #X(F_p) + (2g - 2).
hypotheses: p of good reduction for X
r' < g (e.g. certified rank r < g)
omega with properties (i)-(iii), in particular annihilating J(Q)
proofSteps: (a) If some Q in X(Q) reduces to Qtilde, then by (iii) int_Q^{Q'} omega = 0 for every Q' in X(Q) in the class; as a function of Q' this is a power series I(t) with I' = w, and Lemma 5.1 gives at most m + 1 zeros.
(b) By Riemann-Roch, omega-tilde has 2g - 2 zeros in total, so sum_{Qtilde} m_Qtilde <= 2g - 2 and each m_Qtilde <= 2g - 2 < p - 2. Summing (a) gives #X(Q) <= #X(F_p) + 2g - 2.

Remarks 5.4-5.5 (stated, not proved): an explicit but weaker bound exists for p <= 2g and over number fields ([Col85b] Theorem 4); if r' < g - 1 and p > 2g, #X(Q) <= #X(F_p) + 2r' (Stoll 2006, Cor. 6.7).

Example 8.2: y^2 = x^6 + 8x^5 + 22x^4 + 22x^3 + 5x^2 + 6x + 1 at p = 3 with the Remark 5.2 variant gives #X(Q) <= 6 = #{inf+, inf-, (0, +-1), (-3, +-1)}.

nodes.title: The sieve set A(S, N) in J(Q)/NJ(Q) and its soundness: every rational point maps into A(S, N), so A(S, N) = empty proves C(Q) = empty
nodes.statement: Let C/Q be smooth projective of genus g >= 2 with Jacobian J, iota : C -> J defined over Q (a known rational divisor class of degree 1), and known generators of J(Q). For a finite set S of primes of good reduction and N >= 1, let beta_{N,p} : C(F_p) -> J(F_p)/NJ(F_p) be iota followed by the quotient, alpha : J(Q)/NJ(Q) -> prod_{p in S} J(F_p)/NJ(F_p) the reduction map, and A(S, N) = {a in J(Q)/NJ(Q) : alpha(a) in im(beta_{N,p}) for all p in S}. The diagram with C(Q) -> J(Q)/NJ(Q) on top and prod C(F_p) -> prod J(F_p)/NJ(F_p) at the bottom commutes, so the image of C(Q) lies in A(S, N). In particular A(S, N) = empty implies C(Q) = empty. More generally, with finitely many surjections phi_i : Gamma -> G_i onto finite abelian groups and subsets X_i, and L of finite index in Gamma, A(L) = {gamma in Gamma/L : phi_{L,i}(gamma) in X_{L,i} for all i}; A(N Gamma) is A(S, N) when Gamma = J(Q), G_p = phi_p(J(Q)) inside J(F_p) and X_p = iota(C(F_p)) intersected with G_p.
hypotheses: C/Q smooth projective of genus >= 2 with a known embedding iota defined over Q
known generators of J(Q), or of a finite-index subgroup whose index is coprime to N
S a finite set of primes of good reduction (bad and deep information need Sections 5-6, not read)
proofSteps: Commutativity of the diagram is the compatibility of reduction with iota (Section 2).

If C(Q) = empty is expected, the images of alpha and beta should be disjoint for S and N large enough (Poonen's heuristic and the Main Conjecture of Stoll [St5]). This affects termination only, not soundness.
Section 3.3 closing paragraph: "If we find that A(N_k Gamma) = empty for some k <= m, then we stop. In the context of our application, this means that we have proved that C(Q) = empty as well."
acceptance: The sieve is sound only for the actual group generated by the input points. If they generate a finite-index subgroup, its index must be coprime to N (ED.3 certificate).

Acceptance for ED.5: the certificate records S, N, the groups G_p, the images X_p, the generators and index assumption, and the final set A(S, N). A sieve that has not reached an empty (or fully explained) A(S, N) is an open computation.

nodes.title: Bruin-Stoll Section 3.2-3.3: choose N = q_1...q_m by best-first search on expected sizes and compute A(N_k Gamma) by lifting through intermediate subgroups L_j
nodes.statement: Given Gamma (finitely generated abelian of rank r) and triples (G_i, phi_i, X_i), the expected size of A(L) is n(L) = #(Gamma/L) prod_i #X_{L,i}/#G_{L,i}. Problem 3.2: find N with A(N Gamma) likely empty and computable, and compute it. FindQSequence does a best-first search over sequences of primes q_k with N dividing a bound M (typically M = N_{l-r-1-j} for the invariant factors of prod J(F_p)), such that n((prod q_k)Gamma) < epsilon_1 and max_k n(N_k Gamma) is minimal. Lift(k) computes A(N_k Gamma) from A(N_{k-1} Gamma) through a chain N_{k-1}Gamma = L_0 > L_1 > ... > L_t = N_k Gamma chosen by PrepareLift. Only the indices i with v_{q_k}(e_i) >= v_{q_k}(N_k) (e_i the exponent of G_i) can give new information. At each step an element survives iff phi_{L_j,i}(a' + l) is in X_{L_j,i} for all relevant i.
hypotheses: Gamma, G_i finite, phi_i surjective, X_i subsets given explicitly (products of cyclic groups, images of generators, enumerated subsets)
proofSteps: The correctness of the staged computation is set-theoretic: A(L_j) is exactly the set of lifts of elements of A(L_{j-1}) satisfying the conditions for the indices I_j that change at step j. Elements for i not in I_j satisfy the condition automatically because phi_i(L_j) = phi_i(L_{j-1}). This is stated in the construction of PrepareLift and not isolated as a lemma in the source.
Complexity estimate: sum_j #A(L_{j-1}) (L_{j-1} : L_j), usually about #A(N_{k-1}Gamma) q_k (heuristic, Section 3.3).
The choice of S (Section 3.1) uses primes with B-smooth #J(F_p) and Pohlig-Hellman discrete logarithms; it affects efficiency, not soundness.
acceptance: Check that replacing G_p by the image of J(Q) (not all of J(F_p)) is essential for the expected-size heuristic, as the source warns.

nodes.title: Bruin-Stoll Section 4.2: if N is divisible by the torsion exponent and N^2 > 4H'/m, each coset of NJ(Q) contains at most one point of canonical height <= H'
nodes.statement: Let m be the minimal canonical height of a non-torsion point of J(Q), H' > 0, and N divisible by the exponent of J(Q)_tors with N^2 > 4H'/m. If Q, Q' in J(Q) satisfy Q - Q' in NJ(Q) and hhat(Q), hhat(Q') <= H', then Q = Q'.
hypotheses: canonical height hhat on J(Q) and its minimum m on non-torsion points are known (for genus 2 from Stoll's algorithms [St1, St3], not read)
proofSteps: Source status: stated as a consequence ("These conditions imply") without a written proof.

Unwritten deduction: if Q != Q', then Q - Q' = N R with R in J(Q). If R is torsion, NR = 0 because N kills J(Q)_tors, a contradiction. Otherwise hhat(Q - Q') = N^2 hhat(R) >= N^2 m > 4H'. But hhat(Q - Q') <= 2hhat(Q) + 2hhat(Q') <= 4H' by the parallelogram law, a contradiction.
acceptance: Used to turn A(S, N) into a list of at most one candidate point per coset when searching up to a height bound.

These conditions imply that if Q, Q' in J(Q) are such that Q - Q' in NJ(Q) and hhat(Q), hhat(Q') <= H', then Q = Q'.

nodes.title: Bruin-Stoll Lemma 4.1: a point of J(Q) of canonical height <= H' lying on iota(C(F_{p_j})) for enough primes lies on iota(C(Q))
nodes.statement: Let C be a genus-2 curve, P_0 in C(Q) with x(P_0) = (a : b) coprime integers, iota(P) = [P - P_0], and gamma a bound for h - hhat on J(Q). Let p_1, ..., p_m be primes of good reduction with p_1...p_m > e^{H' + gamma} max{|a|, |b|}^2, such that P_0 and its hyperelliptic conjugate are distinct mod some p_{j_0} if distinct in C(Q). If Q in J(Q) has hhat(Q) <= H' and Q mod p_j lies in iota(C(F_{p_j})) for all j, then Q is in iota(C(Q)).
hypotheses: C of genus 2 with a rational point P_0
naive height h on the Kummer surface and a bound gamma for h - hhat (Stoll [St1, St3])
proofSteps: Let (k_1 : k_2 : k_3 : k_4) be the image of Q on the Kummer surface with coprime integers. If Q mod p_j is on the image of the curve, p_j divides k_1 b^2 - k_2 ab + k_3 a^2.

This integer has absolute value at most e^{H' + gamma} max{|a|, |b|}^2, so divisibility by all p_j forces it to vanish, giving Q = [P - P_0] or [P - Pbar_0] for some P in C(Q); the two cases are separated mod p_{j_0}.
acceptance: Check the Kummer coordinate relation k_1 b^2 - k_2 ab + k_3 a^2 = 0 on a known point [P - P_0].

nodes.title: Bruin-Stoll Section 4.4: if omega_p annihilating J(Q) has nonvanishing reduction on C(F_p) and exp J(F_p) divides N, then C(Q) injects into J(Q)/NJ(Q) and the sieve decides each coset (termination conjectural)
nodes.statement: Let C/Q have genus g >= 2 with Mordell-Weil rank r < g, p >= 3 a prime of good reduction and omega_p in Omega(C_{Q_p}) nonzero, annihilating J(Q), with reduction omega-bar_p not vanishing at any point of C(F_p). (a) Each residue class mod p contains at most one rational point (cited to [St4, Section 6]). (b) If the exponent of J(F_p) divides N, rational points mapping into the same coset of NJ(Q) reduce to the same point of C(F_p). By (a) each coset of NJ(Q) contains the image of at most one rational point. (c) Procedure: find such p; choose S and N with exp J(F_p) dividing N; compute A(S, N); for each a in A(S, N) take the point of smallest canonical height in the coset and check whether it comes from C(Q); otherwise enlarge S or N and recompute on the unresolved elements. If the procedure terminates it returns exactly C(Q).
hypotheses: r < g, generators (or a finite-index subgroup of index prime to N) of J(Q)
p >= 3 of good reduction with omega-bar_p nonvanishing on C(F_p)
a known base point for iota
proofSteps: (a) is imported from Stoll, Independence of rational points on twists of a given curve [St4], Section 6, which was not read. McCallum-Poonen Theorem 5.3(a) gives the same conclusion when m = ord omega-bar_p = 0 < p - 2, i.e. p >= 3.
(b) Reduction mod p factors through J(Q)/NJ(Q) -> J(F_p)/NJ(F_p) = J(F_p) when exp J(F_p) divides N, and iota mod p is injective on C(F_p) for genus >= 1.

Termination is conditional: Steps 4-5 terminate if the Main Conjecture of Stoll [St5] holds for C, and Step 1 succeeds under Conjecture 4.2 (infinitely many good p with nonvanishing omega-bar_p for simple J with r < g). Lemma 4.3 supports Conjecture 4.2 heuristically: a random nonzero regular differential on a genus-g curve over F_p misses C(F_p) with probability at least 1/3 + O(g p^{-1/2}).
acceptance: Correctness (the output equals C(Q) when the procedure terminates) must be separated from termination, which is conjectural (Conjecture 4.2, Stoll's Main Conjecture).
Conjecture 4.4 (deep information) is stated to follow from Matev's p-adic analytic subgroup theorem when the rank is 1; record it as reported, not verified.

sources.excerpt: On the other hand, if N is divisible by the exponent of J(F_p), then the rational points on C mapping via iota into a given coset of NJ(Q) in J(Q) will all reduce mod p to the same point in C(F_p). So if omega-bar_p does not vanish at any point in C(F_p), then we know that each coset of NJ(Q) can contain the image under iota of at most one point in C(Q).

nodes.title: Quadratic Chabauty (BDMTV Section 2): for r = g, log iso and rk NS(J) >= 2, X(Q) lies in the finite set {x in X(Q_p) : h(x) - h_p(x) in Upsilon}
nodes.statement: Let X/Q be smooth projective of genus g >= 2 with Jacobian J of rank r = g, with log : J(Q) (x) Q_p -> H^0(X_{Q_p}, Omega^1)^vee an isomorphism (2.1), X(Q) non-empty with base point b, and rk_Z NS(J) >= 2. A nontrivial Z in Ker(NS(J) -> NS(X) = Z) determines a quotient U_Z of the Q_p-pro-unipotent fundamental group and mixed extensions A(x) = A_Z(b, x) of Galois representations with graded pieces Q_p(1), V = H_1^et, Q_p. Nekovar's p-adic height gives h : X(Q) -> Q_p, bilinear in ([alpha], [beta]) and a sum of local heights h_v. For v != p, h_v has finite image Upsilon_v (Kim-Tamagawa). For v = p, h_p is locally analytic and computed from the filtered phi-module M(x). With Upsilon = {sum_v epsilon_v : epsilon_v in Upsilon_v}, h(x) - h_p(x) is in Upsilon for x in X(Q) (2.3). The extension of h to X(Q_p) via (2.4) makes rho = h - h_p : X(Q_p) -> Q_p a quadratic Chabauty function, Zariski dense on every residue disc, so the set {x in X(Q_p) : rho(x) in Upsilon} is finite and contains X(Q) and the Chabauty-Kim set X(Q_p)_2.
hypotheses: X/Q smooth projective, genus g >= 2, rank J(Q) = g (certified separately)
log J(Q) (x) Q_p -> H^0(X_{Q_p}, Omega^1)^vee is an isomorphism (2.1)
rk NS(J) >= 2, X(Q) nonempty
p a prime of good reduction (for the algorithm, Assumption 3.10)

nodes.title: BDMTV Algorithm 3.12: inputs, steps and FAIL conditions for computing a p-adic approximation of a finite set containing X(Q_p)_2
nodes.statement: Input: a modular curve X/Q with r = g and rk NS(J) > 1 such that the image of J(Q) in H^0(X_{Q_p}, Omega^1)^vee has rank g; a covering of X by affine opens birational to plane curves Q(x, y) = 0 monic in y with p-integral coefficients satisfying Assumption 3.10 (so X has good reduction at p, Remark 3.11); a prime p of good reduction such that the Hecke operator T_p generates End^0(J); local height functions X(Q_l) -> Ker(NS(J) -> NS(X))^*_{Q_p} for all l not of potentially good reduction (Theorem 3.2); a starting precision n; a height bound B. Output: an approximation to precision n' <= n of a finite set containing X(Q_p)_2, or FAIL. Steps: (1) find known points of height <= B; (2) an integral symplectic basis of H^1_dR (or FAIL); (3) Frobenius on H^1_dR by Tuitman's algorithm and T_p via Eichler-Shimura; (4) an End(J)-equivariant splitting of the Hodge filtration; (5) matrices of a basis Z_1, ..., Z_{rk NS - 1} of Ker(NS(J) -> NS(X)); (6) for each Z_i compute lambda_Fil, lambda_phi, solve for the global height pairing from known rational points or Coleman-Gross heights on r independent points (else FAIL), find the zeros of the quadratic Chabauty function(s) (FAIL on precision loss), and FAIL if a non-simple solution corresponds to a known rational point; (7) return the common solutions.
hypotheses: r = g certified a priori (Remark 3.13: for modular curves via Gross-Zagier-Kolyvagin-Logachev and analytic rank one; for hyperelliptic curves possibly by 2-descent)
Assumption 3.10 on the plane models at p
T_p generates End^0(J)
local heights at bad primes supplied externally (Remark 3.16)
proofSteps: The steps and FAIL conditions are those of Algorithm 3.12; Steps (6a)(i)-(ii) follow [BDM+19] Sections 4-5 and are imported.
Remark 3.15: for p ordinary, the unit root splitting is computed as the span of (phi^*)^n eta_{g+1}, ..., (phi^*)^n eta_{2g} mod p^n.

Section 3.4 and Remark 3.8: the returned finite set is compared with X(Q) by the Mordell-Weil sieve (used for the genus-2 examples) or shown to equal X(Q)_known. A finite set of p-adic candidates is not by itself X(Q).
Section 4.4: Proposition 4.6 bounds ord_p(rho_i) >= -2 floor(log_p i) + c_1 + min{c_2, c_3} for i >= i_0, and Lemma 4.7 converts this into provable root precision.
acceptance: Worked examples in the source (not decomposed): X_S4(13), X_0^+(N) of genus 2-3 for prime N, genus-2 curves in Mazur's Program B, C188 and another curve with nontrivial local heights, and X_ns^+(17) of genus 6.

Acceptance for ED.6: each run records the verified rank, the NS-rank condition, the log isomorphism, all local heights, the precision reached, the FAIL status, and the final comparison with global points.
